1.right:
The conquest of the fortress of Constantinople in 1453 AD

(Reign of Mehmed II, 1453 - 1481)
In Peshawar, the Ghazi King Muhammad I also built for the conquest of Constantinople, known as the Anatolian Fortress. When Muhammad II ascended the throne, he also took on a similar ambition. To fulfill this desire, on the European side of the city, he prepared this in three months. Thousands of laborers were put to work. In these three months, he prepared this. On this large tower, a large cannon was placed, and four hundred soldiers were also appointed there, and the order was given that every passing ship should be taxed.
The construction of this fortress began in April 1453. Constantinople is triangular in shape. It is surrounded by water on two sides and land on one side. For this reason, a moat was prepared on the land side, which was one hundred yards wide. The width of the land is six miles. King Constantine, for the purpose of military operations and for the defense of this place, brought Greek soldiers to the moat on his own initiative and threw them at the Turks. But it soon became clear to him that this kind of work was very damaging. After a while, they attacked the fortress walls and from there they would bombard the enemy with arrows and cannonballs. On the other hand, the Turks took shelter from the digging of trenches and slowly advanced. The Sultan's cannon, which was very famous at that time, and the fire of other cannons spread to the fortress walls. And with the slow firing of these cannons, the battlefield was made like the Day of Judgment, and the weak points were broken. In addition, young Turks would go under the gates and reach the edge of the moat.

To fill the ditch, they cut down trees, piled up cannonballs in a heap, and the sacrificing youths created such a commotion that those who were able to see the enemy's strength would fall into the ditch, and in the blink of an eye, they would be buried under piles of dirt. It is said that at that time, death was more desirable than life, as they had already sold themselves for gold. This was the reason why the mother's silence was cast upon herself. The work of the besiegers was to dig the ditch, and the work of the besieged was to clear the ditch, which had become a daily battle. Attacking from the direction of the dam was impossible, as large ships were stationed on the ground on that side. There was a fear that the enemy might attack from the sea. At this time, Sultan Muhammad used his intellect and came up with a strange plan:
He transported his light ships and Turkish equipment across the Bosphorus waters to the dry land, to the large part of the port. The distance between the two seas is ten miles, because the entire area is deep and trees were cut down and stood in places. It was astonishing how, to transport ships on dry land, they built platforms, and on top of them, they placed logs and thick planks so that the ships could be moved. These ships and boats were placed between the Royal Palace and the Alala mountains. It is said that two sailors were on each boat and ship, and they steered themselves. The company's elders and such sons were ready, but the Sultan prepared a single boat in the water and a large cannon.

The wise sayings and words of Saad Zaghloul Pasha

Now, it is happening in the country that the news of the flood's emergence has spread, regarding this, I deemed it appropriate to translate a few wise words of the late Saad Zaghloul Pasha and present them to you, which are very good for the benefit of the field:-

1- Egypt wants complete independence, because this is the inherent right of nations. At this time, we are one reason, but the life of a nation cannot be disappointed by the fate of crushing another nation.

2- Being a humble subject of my nation seems very important to me. Claiming governance over it is a baseless attitude that is harmful.

3- A lover of freedom is not an extremist, because this is the benefit of love. A lover of slavery is an extremist, because slavery is the ultimate humiliation of the self.

4- The spirit of a nation is not something that disappears with laws, nor with oppression, nor with the great empires of the world.

5- O people of the country, it is the duty of all of you to specialize. Saad alone is not responsible; every person of the homeland is responsible.

6- If I say this, it is not my wish. It is not only that there is one nation in Egypt, and the Hindu is only the Egyptian nation.

7- Saad will always be alive even after death, because every Egyptian is Saad, rather, is more than Saad.

8- My life has no envy, no malice. In my soul, the national trust has not given way to anything.

9- Any place that claims to want freedom, has no minimal right.

135.right:
Who are the Pashtuns?

It is stated in many authentic histories that the Pashtuns
are originally Copts and came from Egypt. When Hazrat Musa
Alaihis Salam gained victory over the Pharaoh, the King of Egypt,
many Copts became Muslims. However, one group among them
did not believe in God and His Messenger. Due to extreme
humiliation and ignorance, they left and came to India, and
settled in Koh-e-Sulaiman. Koh-e-Sulaiman is a famous mountain
near the side of the Wazir tribe. Ibn Battuta Maghribi has written
in his history, Tuhfat al-Nuzzar, that Hazrat Sulaiman
came through the path of Sistan to the end. When he was
on this mountain and looked down, India appeared dark to him.
He saw the people of this land as having a dark inner nature,
so he did not like this land. And because of this place...
...this mountain became famous as Koh-e-Sulaiman. When the Arabs
came to this land, they named this sect Sulaimani.
It is the people who live in the mountains of Koh-e-Sulaiman, not that
they are the children of Sulaiman. Abraha, who is
famous as Ashab al-Fil, when he came to destroy Makkah al-Mu'azzamah,
some of these people were also with him, who were killed in Makkah.
During the Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), in the year
when Abdullah bin Amir conquered Khorasan, these people became Muslims.

This Jirga, which included Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Abdul Akbar Khan, Rustam Khan, and other Pashtuns, began in the month of November. In this meeting, it was decided to form the Pashtun "Zalmo Jirga" (Youth Jirga), similar to the "All India Youth League" group in India. The primary purpose of forming this Jirga was to show Pashtuns the path of national unity, independence, and the struggle for their rights. In this meeting, Pashtun leaders emphasized in their speeches that Pashtuns must adopt the path of unity and strive for a common goal. The leaders of this Jirga told the participants that without unity, Pashtuns cannot achieve their rights and must support each other in all circumstances for this goal. Likewise, decisions were made in this meeting to strengthen the cultural and social affairs of the Pashtuns. It is worth noting that the message of unity was spread in the meetings of this Jirga, and it guided Pashtuns to rise as a united force. In the course of this Jirga's work, the need to increase efforts for unity and consensus among the youth in various regions of Pashtunkhwa was mentioned. ---

Although the middle region is mountainous, the mountains are still inhabited, and the land provides all the necessary supplies for a suitable livelihood; there is also plenty of game here—partridges, chukars, and other things are abundant, and at one time the people of this region lived entirely off this. For a long time, the government's attention has been turned toward these people in a crooked way—there is no doubt about it. If they want to hunt, they are fined five rupees per head for many people, and if they want to hunt small game, there is no prohibition; but if they want to hunt in that place, there is no permission for anything unfair, so that they are deprived of the rights of the land, while outsiders hunt freely. May God show favor to these poor Pashtuns, and may God guide their tribal elders not to sell the freedom, peace, prosperity, and honor of their land to others, not to be swayed by the influence of others, and to form their own jirga for the sake of their own reconciliation.

Brothers! We were made targets by those who were arrested and those who were not—they were not put in jail. And how many kinds of cruelties were inflicted upon the poor people of the village. Why was this? After all, what was the fault of the youth? Truly, you will be surprised—that this is not the place—the government does not listen to the truth—so, O Pashtun brothers: what was our fault? That such excess was committed against us.
The truth is that the colonialists do not want this—that this same spirit should be born among us Pashtuns—that we should call the government's right as right and wrong as wrong. The colonialists say that whatever the government orders, the people should trust it blindly. You might say, why do people talk about this today, but listen to me—O brothers! The times have changed. You must know that today in England, there is a rule of the laborers—meaning the power and authority of the kingdom are in the hands of the laborers—but it is a historical fact that in the great assembly (Parliament) of England, one person proposed that laborers should also be given some rights in this assembly. So I ask you, what treatment was meted out to him? He was hanged. Yesterday, they were hanged in the name of laborers and for their rights, and today, the kingdom belongs to them.
Pashtun brothers! The world is changing, and it has changed—but this is not just for us, as I said, that the daughter of Abbas Khan—and the house of Abbas Khan—that we are stuck in those customs, traditions, girls, and enmities—the nonsense... it should have stopped—it was necessary—that for the sake of Abbas Khan, Pashtuns should abandon girls and enmities—become brothers, and recognize the good of your nation and abandon [the bad]—stand up and unite—or else, we will be lost.
After the month of Ramadan, we all came to the Charsadda Tehsil—and there was a strange situation with the government—then from Charsadda, everyone else was released, I was left alone in those circumstances.
When it became evening, my own brother came to tell me about the situation—I asked, why did you not bring the road workers from the village? It became clear that Mr. Willie, the I.C.S. officer who was the Assistant Commissioner at that time—and some days had passed—we also had a settlement—he had stopped the work—I was surprised—that for what reason would he have stopped it? My brother or they themselves came—it became known that some brother police officers had given permission for the road to be entered—I was thankful for their kindness and sympathy—I thought that perhaps the police officers had made some plea or complaint to the Sahib—that Sahib, this is a poor man—his salary is low, he is barely making ends meet—he is a brother—so I also worked well with them—and I paid all their wages with respect—I gave them the answer—that I do not eat the hunger of bribes—look—that you will hear from me again—and I stopped the road—I see—that the next day Willie Sahib came—I asked him—what is the reason for stopping the road? He replied—that the day I was releasing Abbas Khan, he had come to those circumstances.

Pashtun
February 1930

Congress Session in Lahore

Congress is an assembly of the Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, and Christians of India. Once a year, this session is held in one of the provinces of India, and people from all over India gather there. The work of this assembly is to liberate our country (India) from foreigners. These people strive day and night, thinking of ways by which we can be freed from the slavery of foreigners.

This year's session of this assembly was in Lahore. Many foreigners from America, Germany, and England came to watch. It is a pity that this session came so close to our frontier, yet very few people from Pashtun participated.

What should I mention about this session, and if I were to describe it in detail, this entire magazine of mine would be filled, and there would be no room left for other articles. Even then, the pleasure and understanding that I experienced would not be fully conveyed. Therefore, I wish to present to you only the necessary points of this session.

You must be aware that many efforts are being made by this assembly. The British have given us some rights, but since this is our country, it is necessary that we have some share in the government. ---

Recently, he has published a book in the form of a collection of poems as a tribute to the independence of Afghanistan, and has refreshed the memory of the beautiful Pashtun national poet Khushal Khan Khattak. It is a poem of eight-line stanzas. The first part, by the honorable Chiragh, depicts Pashto scenes - the gardens and meadows - and describes the nightingale. The second part speaks with the pain of the great Pashto poet Khushal Khan Khattak, and urges the Pashtun nation to follow in the footsteps of the leaders of this homeland. The writing and printing of the book is very excellent.

Regarding true civilization and education, it is a great necessity for the well-being of the Pashtun and the Pashtun themselves that steps be taken to establish a system at the national level that creates a broad and standard education system for the people of the country. This is a path in which every citizen of the country can obtain their right. For the importance of this education, it is necessary that efforts be made to create a curriculum at the national level that enhances the mental abilities of the people. Its goal should be the promotion of science and knowledge for the progress of the homeland, not just for a specific class. The current system that exists pays attention to the interests of a specific class, due to which many members of our society are left without education. We must try to ensure that education is in accordance with the needs of the people and that every citizen can benefit from the blessing of education in their own country. No matter how many obstacles there are in this path, we must move forward for a bright future and work for the progress of our country in the light of knowledge. Our goal should not just be to build schools, but to create an environment in which everyone has equal opportunity for learning. With this, every individual in our society will participate in the progress of the country and a strong society will be created.
256.left:
A short note on the great need for the development of true civilization and education:

In reality, national education is a necessary step for the common interests of all and the well-being of society. Unfortunately, the current system in the field of education has a series of shortcomings, due to which the people of the country remain deprived of their true right. In these circumstances, a major change is needed in the field of education that will open the doors of knowledge for every citizen of the country. Current education is for a limited circle, while education as a social right should reach everyone. For the development of education, it is necessary that policies be made at the government level that take into account the needs of the people and that practical steps be taken for the progress of the country. In this way, the people of our society will not only be equipped with the light of knowledge, but will also shine in the world as a strong and developed society. It is the duty of every Pashtun to strive for the popularization of education and to raise their voice for this important task.

282.right:

A look at Albania

Albania's (former) King "Ahmed Zogu" is one of those figures of the world who, due to his merit and courage, rose above his ordinary status.

The story of this king's death, Jalal Beg, was among the tribes of Albania. Besides the status of his own business, he was the trusted deputy of Sultan Abdul Hamid. He was born in 1895. Ahmed Zogu was raised in Albania in a way that prepared him for leadership. Until 1915, Albania was part of the Turkish government. But when a freedom movement started against the Sultan's poor governance in Turkey, Ahmed Zogu began to harbor thoughts of his country's freedom. At the age of twenty, he joined the movement. He endured exile, imprisonment, and the hardships of war. Eventually, he succeeded in his goal. In 1924 he became the Prime Minister of Albania, and in 1925 he became the head of Albania. Finally, in 1928, due to his merit and power, he was made King of Albania and took the title "Zogu".

During the time of the freedom movement, he faced many enemies. The people of Albania, like the Wazirs, believe in blood feuds. Controlling these bloodthirsty people was not an easy task. Ahmed Zogu was a brave man. He controlled them with an iron fist. He was always in danger from his enemies. There were reports of him being targeted for assassination over three hundred (300) times. Many attempts were made on his life, but fate protected him, and he remained alive.

He kept his palace protected under the cover of machine guns and often did not participate in public gatherings.

Ahmed Zogu was a very learned man. He could speak German, French, Turkish, and Serbian. He was fond of studying history and spent his lonely nights engaged in work for the betterment of the country.

Zogu was very skilled in maintaining law and order among the people. He brought his enemies under control through his good behavior. Whenever he found out that someone intended to rebel, he would invite them to the palace and bring them under control through his polite behavior.

A priest, Fan Noli, was his very staunch enemy. When Zogu came to power, he exiled him. He lived in America. Finally, he became very ill, and for his treatment, financial ---

Pashtun's message of condolence on the death of Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan
Alas and a hundred times alas that today a great leader like Khan Sahib Khudai Dad Khan, who understood the nation's pain and sorrow, and a fighter for the path of the homeland's freedom who always raised his voice against the oppression and tyranny of the British, is no longer among us. Twelve pieces of advice from Japanese mothers to their daughters at the time of marriage

(1) After the marriage, do not consider your mother-in-law as anything other than your own mother. In fact, consider your mother-in-law as your own mother, and consider all your in-laws as your own, and in any situation, do not upset her.
(2) After the marriage, when you are in someone's land, you must consider their obedience as your duty.
(3) Try so that an opportunity for your mother-in-law to complain about you does not arise.
(4) Do not hold any kind of grudge or enmity with the people of the house. This will ruin your life.
(5) If your husband says something harsh about a matter, do not argue back with him. And try to calm his anger.
(6) Maintain good behavior with your husband's relatives. Do not interfere in every task and his personal affairs.
(7) Wake up early in the morning. And stay awake until late at night. And whatever has passed during the day, do not share it in any gathering.
(8) Manage the household affairs with careful thought. Make it your own habit.

467.right:
In Memory of Tipu Sultan

30
August 1939

In a state where the dark clouds of slavery were spread over many parts of India, in a corner of Indian soil known as Mysore, a shining star rose that lit the lamp of hope for freedom in the hearts of Indians. This shining star was "Tipu Sultan," who had dedicated his entire life to the path of freedom.

Tipu Sultan was not only a wise politician but also a brave military leader. He understood that for the freedom of India, there was a need for an organized and united voice against the British. He established contacts with leaders from various parts of India and urged them to stand against colonialism.

An important part of his life is his confrontation with the British. He defeated the British armies in many battles and halted their expansionist policies. His bravery and perseverance were a source of inspiration for the people of that time.

But unfortunately, due to some traitors and those who sided with foreigners, Tipu Sultan joined the ranks of martyrs in a crucial battle. His death was a great loss to the struggle for India's freedom, but his message and love for freedom remained forever in the hearts of Indians.

In conclusion, we can say that Tipu Sultan's struggle is an excellent example of an untiring effort for the truth. He believed that freedom is the right of every human being and that it is justifiable to make any sacrifice for this right. Although he is not among us today, his achievements and his love for the homeland are written forever in our history.

It is essential for us to learn the lesson from Tipu Sultan's life that we should always have a spirit of sacrifice for the freedom and dignity of our homeland. If we want to leave a dignified and free India for our future generation, then we must follow in the footsteps of such leaders who sacrificed their lives for truth and justice.

This lamp of freedom that Tipu Sultan lit must be kept alive by all of us together today. It is our national duty to keep the memory of such heroes fresh and work for the progress of our country according to their guidance. The soul of Tipu Sultan will be happy when we stand on our own feet for the freedom and survival of our homeland.

540.right:
Pashtun Editorial
This monthly magazine named "Pashtun," which was published in 1929, discusses on this page the importance of unity, brotherhood, and mutual assistance among Pashtuns. At the beginning of the text, a call for Pashtun unity is made, and then the benefits of this and the harms of discord are explained in detail. The text begins as follows:
The benefit of every Pashtun lies in the benefit of the nation; therefore, it is necessary for everyone to join hands. For the progress of this nation, the path of consensus should be taken instead of prejudice. If we unite among ourselves, then no one will dare to look at us with evil intentions. In this article, emphasis is also placed on the importance of knowledge and wisdom, and the youth are urged to strive for education to serve their nation. This article concludes with the slogan of Pashtun national unity.
540.left: In my opinion, if we want to become a strong nation, we must adapt ourselves to the demands of the times while preserving our traditions. In particular, women's education and the training of the youth are what shape our future. In every section of this issue of Pashtun, various stories and advice regarding unity have been written. This magazine presents a vivid picture of the social situation of that time and is a step towards efforts for unity among the Pashtuns. It is hoped that the contents of this magazine will bring about a positive change in the minds of the readers.

However, signs of special measures being taken in response to these actions by Iran are visible. Page 30

11 November 1931

The decision of the Great National Jirga

And the reasons for taking practical steps

A petition

We have received news that in various places, rumors are being spread that a certain group of people has published a document that is having a very negative impact on the people, and such talk is spreading disunity within the nation. Regarding this document, we clarify the following:

(1) Sayyid Abdul Rahman Sahib Kakhail is a person whose words and actions have always been driven by a spirit of goodwill for the nation, and he has always strived for the unity and harmony of the nation; the accusations published against him are baseless.

(2) Mian Attaullah Sahib Kakhail is a person who has always played his intellectual and practical part for the progress of his nation, and the accusations published against him are far from the truth.

(3) With the publication of Karamat Shah Sahib's letter of appreciation for Polad, it became clear that his intention and that of his companions is for the unity of the nation, and he has always remained steadfast on the path of sacrifice for the freedom of the country.

(4) Much more is being said regarding the aforementioned Khan and the document mentioned above, but by looking at his past life and achievements, it is proven that he has always strived for the pride of his nation and has stood firm against all kinds of conspiracies.
574.left:
In this regard, we firmly state that such rumors are spread to create discord among the people and to work for the interests of the colonialists. We call upon all patriots and nationalists not to be deceived by such conspiracies.

It has been decided by the members of the Grand Tribal Jirga that the entire nation will remain united and will work together to achieve independence. We stand against anyone who creates obstacles to the unity of the nation.

Spread this decision in all regions so that all people become aware of the truth. We must maintain an atmosphere of brotherhood among ourselves and not fall into the conspiracies of outsiders.

We are firm in our goal and will not refrain from any sacrifice to achieve independence. The path to freedom is difficult, but with the unity of the nation, this path will become easy.

The Congress Working Committee's Resolution
In the third week of the new month, the resolution passed by the All India National Assembly's Working Committee (Congress Working Committee) in Allahabad is as follows.
Congress, for the sake of its statement, has made clear the policy it has adopted regarding the impact on India and the response it has given to the people of the country. The Working Committee views this policy with satisfaction. This policy has been set forth in statements like those of August 4 and September 1, and in the countless speeches made in various places. Subsequent events and circumstances have justified the evolution and appropriateness of this Congress policy. The nature of the war, and specifically the current policy of Britain and France, and the declarations made by Britain regarding India, indicate that, like the previous general wars, this war is also being fought for imperialistic purposes, and British imperialism seeks to further strengthen its foothold in India. Congress cannot provide any kind of support for this type of war and policy, and it cannot allow the intentions of this purpose to take unfair advantage of the people of India.
